title: One Password, Every Door
performance: given their own work accounts, the viewer can spot a password reused elsewhere, replace it with a unique one kept in a password manager, turn on multi-factor authentication, and deny and report an MFA request or login prompt they did not start

audience.assumed_prior: has several passwords, knows phishing exists, has seen a login code or approval prompt; assumes one leak only costs one account
audience.why: corporate employees in any role who log in every day; no security background
audience.motivation: not wanting to be where a breach started; wants safety without extra hassle
audience.context: work laptop or phone, sound on or captions, short slot between tasks

strategy.name: scenario_led
strategy.rationale: the request is an incident case study; one fictional password followed through one night makes every mechanism concrete before it is named
strategy.signature_move: follow the password one step through the night, show the door it opens, THEN name the mechanism and the habit that would have kept that door shut

misconceptions.belief: a leak on some unrelated personal site only costs that one account
misconceptions.why_tempting: the sites feel unconnected, and the employer's systems were never touched

misconceptions.belief: nobody would bother targeting my password specifically
misconceptions.why_tempting: the employee is not important, so the risk feels personal and small

misconceptions.belief: a long complex password is safe even if I use it in several places
misconceptions.why_tempting: complexity is what password rules usually ask for
misconceptions.source_anchor: F9; not_claimed on complex reused passwords

misconceptions.belief: with MFA on, any approval prompt is safe to accept
misconceptions.why_tempting: the prompt looks official and accepting is one tap

hook.sketch: Late at night, a login to the company system succeeds with the right password. The employee who owns it is asleep.

arc.promise: follow that one password through the night and you will see the two habits that close every door it opened
arc.bridge_from_prior: sec1 opens from what the viewer already does: using the same password on a shopping site and at work

sections.goal: the viewer can explain how a password leaked from an unrelated site ends up opening a work login
the viewer can describe how one valid account lets an attacker reach other systems and accounts
the viewer can apply a unique password per account, a password manager and MFA to decide which step of the attack each habit stops
the viewer can carry out this week's three checks and report a prompt or notice they did not expect

arc.payoff: replay the same night with the habits in place: the leaked password is tried, opens nothing because it is unique, and the second factor holds; the one prompt sent is denied and reported

practice_ladder.what: the narrator walks the password from leak to stuffing to spread, naming each step after it is shown
the same doors appear again; the viewer is asked which habit would keep each one shut before the narrator shows it
an unexpected approval prompt arrives; the viewer decides deny and report before the replay confirms it

recall_moments.prompt_sketch: Two doors: the leaked password tried at login, and a valid account moving on. Which habit shuts which?
recall_moments.answer: a unique password means the leaked one never fits the work login; MFA means even a correct password alone is not enough
recall_moments.tempting_wrong: 'change the password every few months': routine changes without a sign of compromise are not the advice (F16)

recall_moments.prompt_sketch: An approval request you did not start lights up your phone. What do you do?
recall_moments.answer: deny it and report it: it can mean someone already has the password
recall_moments.tempting_wrong: approve it to make it stop

transfer_tasks: this week, list any work password also used elsewhere and replace it with a unique one from a password manager
turn on multi-factor authentication wherever work offers it
the next time an unexpected login prompt, approval request or breach notice arrives, deny it and report it to the security team through your employer's route

persona.voice: a calm investigator walking a colleague through a case file; measured, serious, never dramatic
persona.delivery_notes: low and unhurried in the night scenes; slower on credential stuffing and MFA; plain and brisk on the three actions; no blame in the voice on the reuse

gagne.attention: hook: a successful login at night while its owner sleeps
gagne.objective: promise: follow the password and see the two habits that close its doors
gagne.recall_prior: sec1 bridges from reusing one password at a shop and at work
gagne.present: sections in the order of the attack: leak, try, spread, then the habits
gagne.guidance: signature move: show the door open, then name the mechanism and the habit
gagne.practice: quiz after sec2; recall prompt after sec3; faded doors in sec3
gagne.feedback: quiz answer explained, including why routine changes are not the fix
gagne.assess: the approval prompt in sec4 decided by the viewer before the replay
gagne.transfer: payoff replay and three transfer tasks for this week

merrill.problem_centered: one fictional password's night is the running problem
merrill.activation: sec1 opens from the viewer's own reuse habit
merrill.demonstration: every step is shown happening to the password before it is named
merrill.application: the viewer picks the habit for each door and decides the prompt
merrill.integration: transfer tasks hand the checks to the viewer's own accounts this week

mayer.coherence: one employee, one company, one password; no statistics or side stories
mayer.signalling: the key light lands on the password at each step; slowdowns on the two terms
mayer.redundancy: screen carries the password, doors and a few labels; narration explains
mayer.contiguity: each door opens as its mechanism is spoken
mayer.segmenting: four short sections, one step of the night each
mayer.pre_training: the password as an object and the doors as systems are set up in the hook before the mechanisms run

arcs.attention: a cinematic night and a login nobody made
arcs.relevance: the viewer reuses passwords too; work accounts are theirs
arcs.confidence: two plain habits and a tool that does the remembering
arcs.satisfaction: the replayed night where nothing opens

flags: fictional case only; never a real company or incident
